Model guide · Canon · full-frame mirrorless

Canon EOS R6 V. A full-frame camera built for video first.

Canon announced the R6 V on 13 May 2026. It shares the R6 Mark III’s 32.5 MP resolution and 7K RAW, drops the viewfinder and the mechanical shutter, and adds what Canon highlights for video: a built-in cooling fan, a power-zoom lever and a vertical tripod socket. This guide puts every spec in plain words, says who it suits and lists what to buy with it.

Four things that make it the R6 V.

From Canon’s page, read 26 Nov 2026. Canon’s spec page.

32.5MPFull-frame sensor

Room to crop a 4K frame, and full-frame depth of field for interviews and portraits.

7KRAWUp to 60p, in camera

RAW (Light) at up to 60p, and open gate at 30p to cut horizontal and vertical from one take.

4K120pNo crop

Slow motion that frames like every other mode, so your lens choice doesn’t change.

An internal fan for long recording and streaming; in-body stabilisation up to 7.5 stops with an RF lens.

Specs explained

What Canon says, and what it means for you.

Left: Canon’s spec, as published. Right: what it changes on a shoot.

Canon EOS R6 V specifications (Canon, EOS R6 V product and specifications page, read 26 Nov 2026)
SpecCanon saysWhat it means
Sensor32.5 MP full-frame CMOS, DIGIC XThe same 32.5 MP resolution as the R6 Mark III: room to crop a 4K frame, and full-frame depth of field.
RAW video7K 60p RAW (Light), 17:9, recorded in the cameraRAW keeps everything the sensor saw for grading later. RAW (Light) makes the files smaller than full RAW.
Open gate7K 30p RAW open gate, 3:2: reframe for 16:9, 9:16 or 1:1 laterRecords the whole 3:2 sensor. One take can be cut as a 16:9 film and as a 9:16 vertical for social.
4K 120p4K 120p with no cropSlow motion at 4K that uses the full width of the sensor, so your lens frames the same as at 24p.
Oversampled 4K4K 60p Fine (oversampled); 4K 30p Fine from up to 7KThe camera reads more pixels than 4K and scales down: cleaner, sharper 4K files.
LogCanon Log 2 and Canon Log 3; up to 15+ stops (Canon Log 2, 4K 30p Fine, ISO 800)Flat profiles for grading. Canon Log 3 is the common choice; it matches Canon’s Cinema EOS cameras.
Stabilisation5-axis in-body stabiliser; up to 7.5 stops with a stabilised RF lens (centre)The sensor moves to cancel shake. With a stabilised RF lens the two work together.
CoolingInternal cooling fan, adjustableA built-in fan for long recordings and live streams. Canon lets you set how it runs.
ViewfinderNone: Canon lists no viewfinderYou frame on the screen. If you shoot at eye level or in bright sun, see the R6 Mark III below.
Screen3.0-inch vari-angle LCD, 1.62 million dotsFlips out and turns, so you can see yourself when filming solo.
ShutterElectronic shutter only; up to 40 frames per secondNo mechanical shutter: fast, silent bursts for stills.
FlashFlash not supported (Canon lists flash modes and X-sync as not supported)Not a camera for flash photography. For stills with flash, look at the R6 Mark III.
CardsCFexpress Type B (CFexpress 2.0, VPG400) + SD UHS-IIRAW goes to the CFexpress card; the SD slot can record a 2K proxy or a 4K sub file at the same time.
Audio24-bit audio, up to 4 channelsRoom for two wireless mics and the built-in mic on separate tracks.
ConnectionsFull-size HDMI (Type A), mic in, headphones, USB-C (USB 3.2 Gen 2), E3 remoteFull-size HDMI locks better than micro HDMI on a rig. Headphone and mic jacks on the body.
Webcam4K webcam output (UVC/UAC) over one USB-C cablePlug into a computer and it shows up as a 4K webcam and microphone, no capture card.
PowerLP-E6PLP-E6P batteries; USB-C power or a DC coupler for all-day studio use.
VerticalDedicated vertical tripod socket; the interface rotatesA second tripod socket for portrait framing; the menus rotate with the camera.
Weight688 g with battery and cardReady to shoot with battery and card; 141.8 × 83.3 × 79.7 mm.
Lens mountCanon RF; EF lenses with the EF-EOS R adapterEvery RF lens fits. EF lenses work through Canon’s EF-EOS R adapter.

Source: Canon, EOS R6 V product and specifications page, read 26 Nov 2026. Canon’s regional site for Asia; usa.canon.com refused the automated read on 26 Nov 2026 (HTTP 403).

Who it’s for

Buy it for video. Look elsewhere for these three.

The R6 V is a strong fit for solo creators and small crews. It is the wrong camera for a few jobs.

A good fit

You film more than you photograph.

  • YouTube, documentaries and branded content shot by one person or a small crew.
  • Interviews and podcasts that run long: the fan and USB-C power keep it going.
  • Projects that need both a 16:9 film and vertical cuts: open gate covers both.
  • Live streams through a computer, with the camera as a 4K USB webcam.

Look elsewhere if

You need one of these.

  • A viewfinder or a mechanical shutter: the EOS R6 Mark III ($2,799.00) has both, with the same 7K RAW.
  • A dedicated cinema body: the EOS C50 ($3,899.00) is Canon’s Cinema EOS camera on the store.
  • A first camera under $1,000: the EOS R50 V ($719.00, body).

Canon EOS R6 V questions.

Viewfinder, RAW, the fan, power, cards, EF lenses and streaming.

Does the Canon EOS R6 V have a viewfinder?

No. Canon lists no viewfinder: you frame on the 3.0-inch vari-angle screen (1.62 million dots). If you need one, the EOS R6 Mark III has a 0.5-inch OLED viewfinder and costs $2,799.00 on i9Store (read 26 Nov 2026).

Does the R6 V record RAW inside the camera?

Yes. Canon lists 7K 60p RAW (Light) in 17:9 and 7K 30p RAW open gate in 3:2, recorded to the CFexpress Type B card, with an optional 2K proxy or 4K sub file on the SD card.

Does the R6 V have a cooling fan?

Yes. Canon describes an internal cooling fan for extended recording and streaming, with adjustable fan settings.

What battery and power does the R6 V use?

The LP-E6P battery. Canon also lists USB power through the PD-E2 or PD-E1 adapter, and mains power with the DR-E6P DC coupler plus the PD-E2.

What memory cards does the R6 V take?

One CFexpress Type B card (Canon: CFexpress 2.0 and VPG400 supported) and one SD card (UHS-II supported).

Can I use EF lenses on the R6 V?

Yes, with Canon’s EF-EOS R mount adapter, which Canon lists among the camera’s accessories. RF lenses fit directly.

Can the R6 V work as a webcam?

Yes. Canon lists UVC / UAC streaming: 4K video and audio to a computer over one USB-C cable.
